root.label: Customization points
root.note: How generic code calls the right operation for a type it has never seen.

children.label: ADL two-step
children.note: using std::swap; swap(a, b); lets ADL find a better swap, with std::swap as fallback.

children.label: Qualified call
children.note: std::swap(a, b) suppresses ADL and silently skips the type's own swap.

children.label: Missing using
children.note: Without the using-declaration, ints and types lacking swap fail to compile.

children.label: Hijacking
children.note: Any same-named template in an associated namespace can win or cause ambiguity.

children.label: CPOs
children.note: Const semiregular function objects that do the lookup, check it, and fall back.

children.label: ranges::swap order
children.note: ADL swap with a deleted swap(T&, T&) candidate, then equal-extent arrays, then moves.

children.label: ranges::begin order
children.note: Array, then member begin(), then ADL-only begin(); result must be an iterator.

children.label: ranges::size order
children.note: Array extent, member size(), ADL size(), then end minus begin for sized sentinels.

children.label: P2602 cleanup
children.note: Defect report against C++20 replaced poison pills for begin, end, size with ADL-only wording.

children.label: Why objects
children.note: Objects can be passed around and are immune to ADL.

children.label: ADL suppression
children.note: If unqualified lookup finds a variable, [basic.lookup.argdep] performs no ADL.

children.label: Passable
children.note: ranges::size can be an algorithm argument; most std functions cannot be addressed.

children.label: All instances equal
children.note: Calling a CPO does not depend on the object's value category or constness.

children.label: Niebloids
children.note: The std::ranges algorithms, named after Eric Niebler's range-v3 technique.

children.label: C++20 and C++23
children.note: Not found by ADL, and they inhibit ADL when found by unqualified lookup.

children.label: C++26
children.note: P3136 specifies them directly as algorithm function objects.

children.label: Stricter constraints
children.note: ranges::find needs indirect_binary_predicate; some std::find calls do not port.

children.label: tag_invoke
children.note: P1895: one ADL name for all customizations, with the CPO passed as a tag.

children.label: Costs
children.note: One giant overload set: slow compiles, long errors, hard-to-read definitions.

children.label: Not adopted
children.note: C++26 std::execution moved to member functions and environment queries.

children.label: Customizing today
children.note: Hidden friends for operations; narrow rules for specializing std templates.

children.label: Hidden friends
children.note: Defined in the class, found only by ADL; no conversions from unrelated types.

children.label: Class templates
children.note: Specialize hash, formatter, tuple_size for program-defined types only.

children.label: Type traits
children.note: Specializing <type_traits> templates is UB except common_type and basic_common_reference.

children.label: Function templates
children.note: Specializing them is undefined behavior since C++20 (P0551).
